name: Animated Reaction Captions
visualIdentity: Concise emphasis captions using expressive display lettering, consistent layered outlines, shadows, reaction stickers, and small doodles. Each emotion has its own color and motion. Supplemental, user-requested direction, distinct from continuous subtitles or general kinetic type.
suitableUses: Explicit: descriptive broadcast and reaction-text treatments. Inferred: short vertical clips where brief emphasis words react to speech or faces. Three emotion treatments and 9:16 framing are optional examples, not requirements.
limitations: Faces, dialogue subtitles, and platform overlays must stay unobstructed. Not suited to continuous subtitles or dense text. Reading holds take priority over animation density. Emphasis timing and caption counts are unspecified.
palette: Suggested, not approved; supplied task or brand colors override these. Background #FFF5E5 and foreground #282E3B are layout roles. Accents #DA855C (accent_1), #668FA3 (accent_2), and #A47CA3 (accent_3) map once to the emotions. Foreground on background is 12.592:1; accent_1 with foreground is 4.851:1 for text. accent_2 and accent_3 pairings (3.9 and 3.879) are decorative only. Gradients are disabled and no extra hues may be added.
motionAndInteraction: Short spring entrances, squash, bounce, and wobble fire on reactions or verbal stress, then hold for reading. This style explicitly calls for these, overriding the generic no-bounce default. Video motion derives from seekable composition time. Interactive versions should drop bounce under reduced motion, and hover or pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery.
audio: Audio is unspecified by the style. Music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence are all permissible, and none is mandated. Music timing applies only when a supplied soundtrack, not speech, drives reactions. Speech must stay intelligible and balanced.
assetRequirements: Needs expressive display fonts loaded locally, plus reaction stickers and doodles. Layered outlines and shadows use SVG strokes or aligned text copies. No asset files, exact copy, or motion references are supplied; the reference catalog is optional and empty. Rough.js sketch marks require explicit authorization.
combinations: Usually best used alone, since captions already carry doodles, stickers, and squash. The one suggested pairing is style-105 as a timing system, mapping entrances to precomputed beats of a supplied soundtrack while keeping emotion colors and reading holds. Avoid popping a caption on every beat.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for timing, synchronization, validation, and export; Remotion is a fallback only with a recorded, verified reason. HTML/CSS and SVG are the style renderers, with optional Motion, PixiJS, Rough.js, and mo.js for specific layers. Assign one owner per animated property, seed randomness, and verify seeks and rendered key frames.
